Wimper.et: From Middle High German winbrā, wintprā, variants of Middle High German wintbrā, wintbrāwe, from Old High German wintbrāwa, from wint + brāwa; see Braue for the second component. It has been theorised that the first component may be cognate with Old Prussian w…

Wimpernschlag.et: From Wimper (“eyelash, lash, cilium”) + -n- + Schlag (“flap, beat, hit, blow”).

s: to harvest grapes (for wine); to gather the or a vintage
wimmen.et: From Middle High German wimmen, windemen, from Old High German windemōn, ultimately from Latin vindemiō, itself from vinum + demō.

s: a small, generally triangular flag; a pennant or pennon
Wimpel.et: From Proto-Germanic *wimpilaz; compare Old English wimpel.

s: wine-maker; person who gathers grapes and processes them into wine
Wimmer.et: From wimmen, from Medieval Latin vīndēmiō (“to harvest grapes”).
From wimmen, from Medieval Latin vīndēmiō (“to harvest grapes”).
From Middle High German widemer; related to widmen.

s: hard and knotty area in a piece of wood
Wimmer.et: From Middle High German wimmer, wimer. Further etymology unclear.

s: A picture for children richly detailed with numerous people, animals, and objects.
So kreiert Schlingensief auf Wagners Folie natürlich vor allem ein Wimmelbild, ein monströses, nimmermüdes Tohuwabohu im Neben- und Über- und Durcheinander von Bildern und Tönen.

Of course Schlingensief creates in this way above all a superabundant horror vacui image from Wagner's backdrop, a monstrous, never-tiring vortical chasm in an ensemble of images and notes placed beside, above and through one another.
A genre of painting with many details developed in the 15th and 16th centuries.
to move about in a confused manner and in large numbers
Die Fische wimmeln im Netz herum.
The city is teeming with tourists.
wimmeln.et: From Middle High German wimelen (hapax, 13th c.), frequentative of wimmen, from Old High German wimmen (“to gush, bubble, move lively”). Cognate with Dutch wemelen, Westphalian Low German wiëmeln.

s: A picture book containing pictures richly detailed with numerous humans, animals, and things; wimmelbook.
